title: Collab: consent-gated auto-join when navigating to a #room collab link (joiner complement to task 1354)
description:
USER REPORT (MEDIUM, UX). User opened a shared collab link (#room=...&k=...) and NOTHING happened. They expect navigating to the link to JOIN the session — the standard shareable-link UX. This SUPERSEDES the earlier 'no auto-join is a security feature' framing: the link IS the invitation/capability (the secret k lives only in the fragment, which the inviter chose to share), so navigating to it is a deliberate join intent. (USER-CONFIRMED INTENT.)

CONFIRMED IN CODE — nothing reads location.hash at mount:
- parseCollabLink (packages/authoring-ui/src/collab/collabLink.ts:111) is invoked from EXACTLY ONE place: ShareDialog.tsx:261 (the dialog's explicit Join button, onJoin → parseCollabLink(joinInput)). grep of the whole authoring-ui/desktop tree for location.hash / hashchange / popstate shows NO mount-time fragment read driving a join.
- collabUrl.ts WRITES the fragment (writeCollabFragment) on Start/Join and CLEARS it on Leave (task 1354), and parseCollabLink is also called inside clearCollabFragment to detect OUR fragment — but no code path READS the fragment at app load to initiate a join. So a freshly-navigated #room link is inert: CollabContext.start/join only run from explicit user actions in the dialog/controls.
- Task 1354 (DONE) explicitly recorded the decision 'No auto-join-on-load: parseCollabLink is still invoked ONLY from the dialog's explicit Join; nothing reads location.hash at mount.' THIS TASK reconciles/supersedes that decision per user-confirmed intent. 1354 is the HOST half (write room URL on Start); this is the JOINER half (act on a navigated #room link) — together they form the full collab-link round-trip.

FIX DIRECTION (NOT applied — code untouched). Mount-time fragment detection → CONSENT prompt → join (NOT silent auto-connect):
1) On app load (a mount-time effect, ideally in CollabProvider/CollabContext.tsx or a small new hook beside it), read window.location.hash and run parseCollabLink on it. If it parses to a CollabLink AND there is no live session yet → it is a join invitation.
2) Show a CONSENT prompt (e.g. a modal: 'Join collaborative session?' with Join / Dismiss), reusing the ShareDialog HonestNote disclosure (ShareDialog.tsx HonestNote — collaborators connect peer-to-peer over WebRTC so IPs are mutually visible). Do NOT silently auto-connect: the joiner exposes their IP/presence to the other participants, so the join must be INFORMED. The link is the capability; the consent click is the informed-exposure gate.
3) On confirm → call the existing CollabContext.join(link) (which already wires joinCollab + writeCollabFragment to keep the address bar canonical). On dismiss → optionally clear the fragment (clearCollabFragment) so a reload doesn't re-prompt, or leave it and let the Share dialog's Join field pre-fill from it.
4) Gate on COLLAB_ENABLED_DEFAULT / the collab feature flag (store/collabFlag.ts) — if collab is disabled, do not prompt.
5) Guard against double-handling: the fragment WE write on Start/Join (collabUrl.ts) must not re-trigger the prompt. Run the mount detection ONCE before any session exists (e.g. only when session === null on first mount), and/or ignore the fragment if a session is already live. The 1354 write uses replaceState after join, so ordering the mount-read before the first write avoids a self-join loop.

DESIGN NOTES:
- Consent prompt, not silent connect: chosen deliberately (informed IP/presence exposure). The link grants the capability; the click confirms the human chose to expose themselves to that specific room.
- Reuse existing pieces: parseCollabLink, CollabContext.join, ShareDialog.HonestNote copy, collabUrl helpers. No new transport.
- Acceptance: navigate to a real #room=...&k=... URL → consent modal appears → Join → session connects (presence/peer count updates) and the address bar stays the room link; Dismiss → no connection. jsdom/unit test the mount-detection helper purely (inject window.location.hash + a mock join); an e2e can drive the two-tab Start→copy-URL→open-in-second-context→consent→Join round-trip.

Related: task 1354 (host URL reflection — DONE; this is its joiner complement / reconciles its no-auto-join note), task 1356 (default signaling), task 1355 (relay hardening).
